key_insight: Cluster-TNN scales topological deep learning by lifting graph structure locally inside mini-batches instead of materializing the full higher-order domain upfront.
engineering_relevance: This makes higher-order neural models practical on large, dense graphs by sharply cutting GPU memory while preserving competitive accuracy.
method: Partition the input graph during preprocessing into clusters.
At runtime, sample clusters and rebuild their induced subgraphs as mini-batches.
Apply the chosen topological lifting within each mini-batch to form processable higher-order structures.
evidence_signal: Across 21 matched comparisons, Cluster-TNN reduced peak GPU memory in every case, averaging 83.2% less memory while maintaining competitive predictive performance, including on Reddit and OGBN Products.
watch_item: Performance may depend on partition quality and on whether local mini-batches preserve enough cross-cluster connectivity to reconstruct meaningful higher-order structure.
paper_title: Batch Before You Lift: Scalable Topological Deep Learning on Large Graphs
